Report_ID: Acute kidney injury (radiocontrast nephropathy) incidence at 48 hours
Title: Fenoldopam mesylate blocks reductions in renal plasma flow after radiocontrast dye infusion: A pilot trial in the prevention of contrast nephropathy
Author: Tumlin JA, Wang A, Murray PT, Mathur VS
Comment: Event counts are not stated verbatim; the paper reports only percentages. Counts were back-computed from the explicitly reported per-arm percentages and randomization Ns (41.0% x 22 = 9.0 events; 21.0% x 23 = 4.8 ≈ 5 events), consistent with the stated overall incidence of 29.5% (14/45 ≈ 31%). Denominators are the randomized Ns from Table I (1/2 NS n=22, FNP n=23). Note the Results text elsewhere inconsistently refers to the fenoldopam group as "14 of 25" diabetics, while Table I lists n=23.
Participant type: adult patients with chronic renal insufficiency (serum creatinine 2.0-5.0 mg/dL) undergoing coronary or peripheral contrast angiography
Recruitment source: inpatient and outpatient angiography at participating centers
Outcome measurement: Dichotomous: number of patients in whom RCN developed / total randomized per arm (reported as percentages)
Outcome variable: Acute kidney injury (radiocontrast nephropathy) incidence at 48 hours

Report_ID: Incidence of acute kidney injury (cases of ARF)
Title: Prophylactic fenoldopam for renal protection in sepsis: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial
Author: Morelli A, Ricci Z, Bellomo R, Ronco C, et al.
Comment: Fisher's exact test p-value reported; no test statistic given. Odds ratio 0.47 is adjusted (logistic regression), not a crude risk ratio; coefficient -0.72 (p = .01) stored in M_diff as the regression log-odds coefficient for treatment. Reported effect measure field left blank per rules (paper names an odds ratio for the adjusted model only).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Fenoldopam 0.09 µg·kg-1·min-1') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: septic ICU patients with baseline serum creatinine <150 µmol/L
Recruitment source: Three multidisciplinary intensive care units at a university hospital
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of patients developing serum creatinine >150 µmol/L during study drug infusion
Outcome variable: Incidence of acute kidney injury (cases of ARF)

Title: High-dose fenoldopam reduces postoperative neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocaline and cystatin C levels in pediatric cardiac surgery
Author: Ricci et al.
Comment: The paper reports only percentages (50% vs 72%), not raw event counts; with ITT denominators of 40 per arm this corresponds to 20/40 in group F and ~28.8/40 (i.e. about 29/40) in group P. Event-count fields were left empty because the exact counts are not stated verbatim. Trial was explicitly not powered for AKI incidence.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group F – fenoldopam 1 µg/kg/min during CPB') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: infants <1 year with congenital heart disease undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB
Recruitment source: tertiary pediatric hospital (Bambino Gesù Children's Hospital, Rome)
Outcome measurement: Proportion of patients classified in any pRIFLE class (Risk/Injury/Failure)

Report_ID: Incidence of acute kidney injury (radiocontrast-induced nephropathy)
Title: Prospective Randomized Study of N-Acetylcysteine, Fenoldopam, and Saline for Prevention of Radiocontrast-Induced Nephropathy
Author: Allaqaband et al.
Comment: Event counts not reported directly as counts in Table II; derived as 15.7% × 38 ≈ 6 (fenoldopam) and 15.3% × 40 ≈ 6 (saline), corroborated by Table III diabetic-status stratification (fenoldopam 4/2 = 6; saline 3/3 = 6; NAC 5/3 = 8; total 20 = stated total RCIN cases). The reported P = 0.919 is a 3-group omnibus test, not the pairwise fenoldopam-vs-saline comparison.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Fenoldopam 0.1 µg/kg/min i.v. (4 hr pre + 4 hr post) plus 0.45% saline') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: High-risk patients with chronic renal insufficiency (baseline creatinine > 1.6 mg/dl or creatinine clearance < 60 ml/min) undergoing cardiovascular procedures with radiocontrast
Recruitment source: Aurora-Sinai Medical Center, patients scheduled for cardiovascular interventions
Outcome measurement: Proportion of patients with serum creatinine rise >= 0.5 mg/dl at 48 hr
Outcome variable: Incidence of acute kidney injury (radiocontrast-induced nephropathy)
additional_group_ns: N-acetylcysteine 600 mg orally twice daily plus saline, n = 45 (RCIN 17.7%, 8 events) — arm not part of the fenoldopam-vs-control comparison

Author: Cogliati AA, Vellutini R, Nardini A, Urovi S, Hamdan M, Landoni G, Guelfi P

Report_ID: Contrast-induced nephropathy (AKI): serum creatinine increase of >=25% within 96 hours postprocedure
Title: Fenoldopam Mesylate for the Prevention of Contrast-Induced Nephropathy: A Randomized Controlled Trial (CONTRAST)
Author: Stone GW, et al. (CONTRAST Investigators)
Comment: Denominators are the evaluable-creatinine populations (137 fenoldopam, 146 placebo) rather than total randomized (157 and 158), because serial creatinine was unavailable in ~10% of randomized patients. Paper reports sensitivity analyses were unchanged but does not give imputed counts.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Fenoldopam mesylate IV 0.05-0.10 µg/kg/min + hydration') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults with creatinine clearance <60 mL/min undergoing diagnostic and/or interventional cardiac angiographic procedures
Recruitment source: 28 academic and community-based centers in the United States, March 2001 - July 2002
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of patients with serum creatinine increase >=25% from baseline to maximum value within 24-96 h
Outcome variable: Contrast-induced nephropathy (AKI): serum creatinine increase of >=25% within 96 hours postprocedure

Title: Use of Fenoldopam to Control Renal Dysfunction Early After Liver Transplantation
Author: Biancofiore et al.
Comment: The reported P = .7 is the omnibus chi-squared across all three groups; no pairwise fenoldopam-vs-placebo test statistic is reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group F: fenoldopam 0.1 µg/kg/min IV infusion') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)

Report_ID: Acute kidney injury (RIFLE criteria), total population
Title: Effects of fenoldopam infusion in complex cardiac surgical operations: a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study
Author: Ranucci M, De Benedetti D, Bianchini C, Castelvecchio S, Ballotta A, Frigiola A, Menicanti L
Comment: Denominator in the fenoldopam arm is 38 (not the 40 randomized) because 2 preoperative chronic-dialysis patients were excluded from renal secondary endpoints, as stated in the Results and Table II footnote. Zero events in the fenoldopam arm — zero-cell handling required for RR pooling.
Study Environment: clinical / hospital operating theatre and ICU
